title: Conformance snapshot
description: How far a repository's tree is from its architecture manifest, as `architecture conformance --json` reports it. See https://dataquail.github.io/goodbones/architecture-rules/enforcement/conformance/.

path.description: The file the policy was read from — the root file, when split with `include`.

sha256.description: A hash of that file's bytes, so two snapshots can say whether the policy changed between them.

manifest.description: The policy this snapshot was taken against — the repository's own, or the one `--against` named.

conformance.description: Per measure, the count `check` holds to the manifest's `limits.conformance`: residue files, vacant nodes, slack allowances, and fragment entries used at fewer than half the nodes granted them. The lists below name what each counts.

folders.description: Folders every walked file of which is residue, each the topmost such folder.

residue.description: What the policy has nothing to say about. A file in an open folder under no allowlist is claimed, not policed, and counts.

allOf.description: Distinct entries the node wrote, `allow` and `external` together.

vacant.description: Nodes that state an import allowlist and select no walked file, in manifest order. Every allowance on one is unused by construction, so none is counted as slack; the node is a tier declared ahead of its first file, or a pattern that no longer matches. Residue is files no node reaches; this is nodes no file reaches.

fingerprint.description: kind|rule|file|subject — line-independent, so it survives edits to the file it names; the baseline's key.

ruleName.description: The manifest node path the rule was lowered from.

subject.description: The other end of the violated relationship — the resolved target, the restricted symbol, the missing sibling — or null when the file alone is the violation.

baselined.description: Carried by the baseline, so `check` does not fail on it.

ledgered.description: For a campaign hit: carried by the objective's ledger, so `check` does not fail on it.

objective.description: For a campaign hit: the objective that fired.

sector.description: For a campaign hit: the sector the hit falls in.

entry.description: For a campaign hit: its ledger entry, relative to the sector's root.

violations.description: Every finding, baselined ones included, ordered so the ones cheapest to fix come first: by the height of the violated target in the import graph, leaves first.

unresolved.description: Imports the resolver could not turn into a file. Every rule about one enforces nothing.

stale.description: Baseline entries the code no longer produces.

allOf.description: Entries in the baseline file.

baseline.description: The debt the policy is carrying. The ratchet: it may only shrink.

allOf.description: Strongly connected components of more than one file, or a file importing itself, anywhere in the walked graph — in a cycles rule's scope or not.

node.description: The manifest node that wrote the entry — or, when `fragment` is set, the `defs` fragment it was written in.

kind.description: `allow` is a path glob under `imports.allow`; `external` a package name under `imports.external`.

entry.description: The entry as written, after alias expansion.

fragment.description: Present when the entry arrived through `use`. The nodes that referenced the fragment wrote one word, so the entry is reported once, against the fragment, rather than once per node.

allOf.description: With `fragment`: how many non-vacant nodes were granted the entry through it. None of them uses it.

slack.description: Allowances no observed import uses, in manifest order, vacant nodes excluded. A manifest inferred from the tree has none on the day it is written; every entry here is permission nothing needs. An entry that arrived through `use` is reported once, against the fragment, and only when no node granted it uses it.

fragment.description: The `defs` fragment the entry was written in.

kind.description: `allow` is a path glob under `imports.allow`; `external` a package name under `imports.external`.

entry.description: The entry as written, after alias expansion.

allOf.description: Nodes granted the entry through the fragment that use it.
Non-vacant nodes granted the entry through the fragment.

concentration.description: Fragment entries used at some of the nodes granted them and not the rest. Not slack — the fragment's line is needed somewhere — but a per-file permission written as a many-node allowance, which is what an allowlist widened to make one build green looks like.

adoption.description: The tiers that said "not tightened yet", by name; `limits` caps how many may.

id.description: The campaign's id; its ledgers are under `<ledger>/<id>/`.

title.description: The campaign's title, when it states one.

owner.description: Who is running the campaign, as the manifest names them.

allOf.description: Holdouts across every objective and sector.
Cleared over everything ever ledgered, across the campaign's objectives.

id.description: The objective's id; its ledger is `<ledger>/<campaign>/<objective>.json`.

phase.description: The phase naming the objective, or `null` for one no phase names — in window everywhere.

allOf.description: Holdouts recorded as each sector entered the window, summed.
Holdouts added since by `objectives concede` or a re-baseline, each with a concession.
Holdouts in the ledger now, every sector summed.
Holdouts removed by `objectives clear` because they stopped firing.
Holdouts still firing when a sector left the window — not progress.
`1 - count / (initial + allowed - closed)`: how much of everything ever ledgered has been paid down.

lastCleared.description: When a holdout last left the ledger, ISO 8601 — the stall clock's reading; `null` with no ledger.

allOf.description: How many times a count was allowed to go up.

ledgered.description: Whether a ledger exists. An objective with none has been declared and not yet cleared.

defined.description: Whether the phase names criteria. An open phase has only an intent, and is last.

allOf.description: How many sectors are derived to stand at this phase.

phases.description: The ladder, in order, with how many sectors stand at each phase.

name.description: The sector's identity, as its perimeter names it.

phase.description: The phase the sector is derived to stand at, or `null` when it is past the last one.

reached.description: The furthest phase the sector's record says it has reached; `null` before its first `clear`.

allOf.description: How many files the sector claims.

residue.description: One dimension per objective in window for the sector: its holdouts there, never summed.

stalled.description: Holdouts remain for the sector and nothing has been cleared, attested or noted within `staleAfter`.

sectors.description: Every sector the perimeter births, by name.

allOf.description: Files in the scope no sector claims.
Holdouts in the legacy, under the first phase's objectives — where a holdout moved out of a sector lands.

legacy.description: The unclaimed remainder of the scope, which stands at the first phase and is not a sink.

refined.description: Phases refined since the last `clear`: an open phase that gained criteria, or a new one. Free.

changed.description: Defined phases whose definition changed since the last `clear` — what a reviewer reads every time.

unreceipted.description: Changed phases carrying no new concession; `check` fails on them.

plan.description: What changed in the plan, refinements and changes apart.

stalled.description: Holdouts remain and nothing has been cleared, attested or noted within the campaign's `staleAfter`.

complete.description: No holdouts remain in any objective.

onComplete.description: What the manifest asks once complete: keep the campaign as a guard, or remove it.

ledgered.description: Whether every objective has a ledger.

campaigns.description: Every campaign the manifest declares, in manifest order, with its burn-down. Campaign hits are not counted in `coverage` or `residue`: a campaign is scoped by construction.
